questions.question: Which of the following interchanges of numbers (not digits) would make the given equation correct? \(\frac{480 \div 0.3 \times 5 + 500}{190 + 9 \times 27 \div 1.6} = 2 \)
questions.questionHtml:
Which of the following interchanges of numbers (not digits) would make the given equation correct?
\(\frac{480 \div 0.3 \times 5 + 500}{190 + 9 \times 27 \div 1.6} = 2 \)
questions.solution:
Option  2): 0.3 and 1.6

\(\frac{480 \div 0.3 \times 5 + 500}{190 + 9 \times 27 \div 1.6} = 2 \) ⇒ \(\frac{480 \div 1.6 \times 5 + 500}{190 + 9 \times 27 \div 0.3} = 2 \)

⇒ \(\frac{300 \times 5 + 500}{190 + 9 \times 90} = 2 \) ⇒ \(\frac{1500 + 500}{190 + 810} = 2 \) ⇒ \(\frac{2000}{1000} = 2 \)

⇒ 2 = 2 (LHS = RHS)

questions.question: Six letters A, B, C, E, F and G are written on different faces of a dice. Two positions of this dice are shown in the figure below. Find the letter on the face opposite to A.
questions.questionHtml:
Six letters A, B, C, E, F and G are written on different faces of a dice. Two positions of this dice are shown in the figure
below. Find the letter on the face opposite to A.
questions.solution:
As A is common on both the dices, it is clear that B, C, G, and F are adjacent to it, and the remaining i.e. E will be opposite to it.

Opposite pairs:

B → F, C → G, A → E

questions.questionHtml:
In a certain code language,
X + Y means ‘X is the father of Y’,
X − Y means ‘X is the brother of Y’,
X × Y means ‘X is the sister of Y’,
X ÷ Y means ‘X is the wife of Y’.
Based on the above, how is D related to H if ‘D × E ÷ F + G − H’?
questions.solution: Thus, D is H's mother’s sister or maternal aunt.
